belvidere: Before replacing a visible exterior feature, check whether your property is in Belvidere’s historic district. The Town provides a district map and application information; the property’s age alone does not tell you which review applies.
hope: If exterior work may involve historic review, check Hope’s current application process before ordering replacement materials. Confirm whether it applies to your property and proposed change.
plainfield: For a designated historic property, discuss repairing the existing feature before choosing a replacement. Plainfield’s preservation resources can help you prepare; confirm the property’s status and the review needed for your specific work.
mountain-lakes: Mountain Lakes provides a restoration handbook with guidance for original Hapgood and Belhall homes. If you want to preserve an existing detail, it can be a useful starting point when comparing repair and replacement options.
rockleigh: Rockleigh publishes Historic Roadway Design Guidelines. If your project affects a feature along a historic roadway, ask the Borough whether those guidelines or another review apply before finalizing the work. Do not assume they govern every exterior repair.
westfield: If your property is locally designated historic, use Westfield’s design and application resources when discussing an exterior change. The appearance or age of a house alone does not establish its status.
maplewood: For yard cleanup, agree on equipment and debris removal in the quote. Maplewood publishes leaf-blower restrictions, so the professional should check the current rules for the equipment and planned date.
mount-olive: The Mount Olive recycling depot has an accepted-materials list and resident-access requirements. Check the list before choosing a drop-off route; a garage clear-out may include items that need separate hauling.
newark: Newark’s collection guidance excludes construction debris from municipal bulk pickup. Keep renovation material separate from unwanted furniture in your removal request and agree who will haul it away.
new-milford: New Milford’s Recycling Center does not accept trash or bulky items under the Borough’s published guidance. Check the current collection options or include hauling in your clear-out request.
moonachie: If you are disposing of a refrigerator or air conditioner, Moonachie publishes a special curbside-permit process for those items. Confirm the current collection requirements and arrange any necessary disconnection before scheduling removal.
riverdale: Riverdale lists different disposal routes for metal appliances, electronics and hazardous waste. Identify each item before choosing removal or drop-off, and agree who handles any disconnection.
northvale: Northvale’s Public Works guidance says landscapers and tree companies may not leave their debris at the curb for pickup. Make removal part of the professional’s quote.
ridgefield: Ridgefield’s collection guidance separates areas east and west of Shaler Boulevard and treats branches separately. Check the current calendar or agree that the professional will remove the material.
roxbury: Roxbury separates grass, leaves and brush in its yard-waste guidance. Agree whether the professional will haul material away or prepare it for the appropriate collection; yard waste should not be blown into the street.
secaucus: Secaucus provides separate applications for dumpsters and portable storage containers. Decide whether you need disposal or temporary storage, then check current placement requirements before arranging a container.
mahwah: Mahwah publishes tree-removal guidance and a tree-service vendor-registration resource. Before arranging tree work, check the current requirements for the property and professional; an A5 match does not establish local registration.
waldwick: Waldwick has separate tree-removal and tree-contractor registration processes. Confirm the current requirements before scheduling; an A5 match does not establish the professional’s local registration.
paramus: For a tree near the curb or sidewalk, check whether it is a Borough tree before arranging work. Paramus Shade Tree & Parks is the local starting point for Borough-tree questions.
rutherford: Rutherford directs street- and park-tree concerns to its public works and shade-tree offices. Clarify responsibility before combining public-tree work with a private path or landscaping repair.
hawthorne: If the repair involves the sidewalk along the street, distinguish it from a private garden path in your request. Hawthorne’s Building Department issues sidewalk permits; check the requirements for the proposed work before agreeing on the scope.
hillside: Hillside provides a sidewalk-replacement application. If your project involves the street-facing sidewalk, check the current process and include access and restoration in the professional’s proposal.
haworth: For driveway work, say whether you are keeping the existing footprint or changing it. Haworth’s guidance distinguishes replacement from modifications, so confirm the applicable process before agreeing to an expansion.
montville: For work near the street, show the repair area in relation to the curb, sidewalk and driveway. Montville’s Engineering Department handles right-of-way and lot-grading questions that may affect the project. Confirm the applicable requirements before changing the layout.
washington-township-warren: If a tree or drainage concern crosses the property edge, clarify who is responsible for the road before arranging private work. Washington Township’s Public Works resource distinguishes Township, county and state roads.
hanover-township: Whippany and Cedar Knolls mailing references can be included with your request, but identify Hanover Township as the work municipality. Hanover Township and East Hanover are separate municipalities.
boonton: Town of Boonton and Boonton Township are separate municipalities. Use the work property’s municipality in your request, even when the mailing address is similar.
boonton-township: Boonton Township and Town of Boonton are separate municipalities. Identify the work property as Boonton Township in your request to help keep the location clear.
chatham-borough: Chatham Borough and Chatham Township are separate municipalities. Include the work property’s municipality and ZIP code so the request is associated with the right location.
chatham-township: Chatham Township and Chatham Borough are separate municipalities. Include the work property’s municipality and ZIP code so the request is associated with the right location.
andover-borough: Andover Borough and Andover Township are separate municipalities. Include Andover Borough and the property’s ZIP code in your request.
andover-township: Andover Township and Andover Borough are separate municipalities. Include Andover Township and the property’s ZIP code in your request.
washington-township-bergen: This page is for Washington Township in Bergen County. Include the county in your request to distinguish it from the Washington Townships in Morris and Warren counties.
washington-township-morris: This page is for Washington Township in Morris County. Include the county in your request to distinguish it from the Washington Townships in Bergen and Warren counties.
